note: Legacy money columns stored as REAL dollars rather than INTEGER cents. Recorded, not fixed: converting them is a data migration over live fiduciary records — LP commitments, capital calls, distributions, NAV, portfolio marks — not a lint fix, and it needs a product decision about rounding and about which of the two dialects each surface reads. What this ledger buys is that the split stops growing: the gate fails on a NEW float money column, and equally on an entry here that has since been converted, so the list cannot go stale. The schema already speaks both dialects — 31 *_cents INTEGER columns exist and every one is correctly typed.
convert_with: a migration adding <col>_cents INTEGER, a backfill of ROUND(<col> * 100), and a cutover of every reader; do not drop the REAL column in the same migration.

columns.project_metrics.arr: CARRIED OVER, NOT NEWLY DECIDED. Migration 249 moved the per-project metric series out of metrics_snapshots — which is the per-DEAL traction table and never had project_id, mrr, active_users, notes or source, so routes/progress.ts's KPI form and stripe.ts's MRR sync both threw 'no such column: project_id' (#203, D87). These four figures are the SAME four this ledger already records against metrics_snapshots, in the same denomination, with the same readers; the split does not grow here, it changes address. WHY NOT CENTS IN A BRAND-NEW EMPTY TABLE, which is the fair question: because the denomination is not the table's to choose alone. services/saasMetrics.ts computes LTV:CAC, CAC payback, burn multiple, CMGR and runway over these as dollars; financial_models.assumptions_json carries mrr and arr as dollars beside them; and the SPA renders both. Converting the column without converting that whole chain would put two denominations one join apart, which is worse than either. Re-denominating the metric series is its own task with its own product decision about rounding. Note metrics_snapshots.mrr's entry is now doubly stale: the deal table never had that column, and the only CREATEs that declared it were the two writers' own — the union limitation check-sqlite-columns documents.
